findings.title: Overlapping ownership of BSVoiceCAD.Orchestrator.Agent namespace
findings.location: Section 1. Module Map table, rows SPEC-03 and SPEC-05
findings.problem: Two modules claim ownership of the identical namespace while the document asserts "Dependency direction is strictly downward" and "Circular references are a defect."
findings.why_it_matters: Creates immediate governance conflict during parallel implementation, violating the integration contract purpose of "well-defined seams".
findings.proposed_fix: Partition Agent subcomponents into distinct namespaces owned by exactly one spec; update table and all seam descriptions.

findings.title: Document violates its own "names nothing else" boundary
findings.location: Section 0. Why This Exists (including Non-goals paragraph)
findings.evidence: "This document names the modules, names the seams, and names nothing else." and explicit non-goals listing "state machine details, record field definitions, ... build sequence, timeline"
findings.problem: Sections 3, 4 (7 SDR-TL entries), 5, 6 (detailed glossary), and 7 introduce mandatory scope, licensing, regulatory framing, review ordering, and build blockers.
findings.why_it_matters: Defeats the isolation promise that "Oracle reviews each module spec in isolation" and inflates complexity of the integration contract itself.
findings.proposed_fix: Strip all non-seam content to a separate ADR or move into the lowest dependent module spec; rewrite Section 0 to match actual contents.

findings.title: Brittle dependency on undefined Opus 4.7 model behaviors
findings.location: SDR-TL-008 and Glossary entries for Vision Context, Ambiguity Event, Turn type
findings.evidence: "Opus 4.7's internal self-verification at xhigh effort is the model-level consensus mechanism", "Vision interpreter (context-only...)", "turn_type = 'ambiguity_resolution' with both the transcript and the vision context observations preserved"
findings.problem: Core seams (D, E, C) and DHF schema assume specific future model capabilities (structured vision output, reliable self-verification) that do not yet exist and may never materialize exactly as described.
findings.why_it_matters: If opposite assumption is true (model hallucinations in vision, inconsistent structuring), the entire lifecycle, quarantine, and ledger rules collapse, requiring rework across SPEC-03/04/05. Speculative but high-impact.
findings.proposed_fix: Decouple architecture from any specific model version; define explicit contracts for vision enrichment and ambiguity detection that can be satisfied by multiple providers or fallback logic.

findings.title: Omission of concrete cross-process transport mechanism
findings.location: Seam B, Seam D, SDR-TL-001, and references to WebSocket in Section 6 Glossary
findings.evidence: "SPEC-02 provides a synchronous method surface; SPEC-03 wraps each call in its own timeout and cancel semantics." "The agent never touches the WebSocket, never touches the STA queue"
findings.problem: .NET Framework 4.8 STA add-in and .NET 8 orchestrator require an IPC layer; document never names the actual transport, serialization beyond JSON policy, or error mapping across process boundaries.
findings.why_it_matters: Makes claimed one-directional synchronous dispatch unimplementable and untestable. NetArchTest rules cannot enforce what is not specified. Direct cause of integration failure.
findings.proposed_fix: Add explicit seam definition (e.g. named pipes, gRPC, or JSON-RPC over stdio) in SPEC-01 and reference it from every cross-process seam; include error semantics and threading guarantees.
